title: Hub management
description: The workstations and servers paired with this hub. Each device acts as the user it was paired for.

devices.label: Devices
devices.outdatedHint: Its connector isn't on the hub's version. It updates itself when it connects.
devices.failedRollback: Version {{version}} did not start on the device, so it went back.
devices.emptyBody: Pair a device so its connector can work with this hub.
devices.name: Name
devices.revokeBody: The device loses access at once. Its local files stay on its disk. To use it again, pair it with a new code.

sync.paused_other: Sync paused: {{count}} files deleted in {{roots}} at once. Choose what happens to them below.

edit.portHint: The connector's page on its own computer. A new port applies after a restart.
edit.autostartHint: Starts the connector when you log in.
edit.restartRequired: Saved. Restart the connector to use port {{port}}.
edit.offline: The connector is offline, so it didn't get this.
edit.outdated: This connector is too old for this. Update or restart it on its computer, then try again.
edit.timeout: The connector didn't answer. Try again.
edit.offlineNote: The connector is offline. This can only be changed while it is online.
edit.restarting: Restarting. It shows online again in a few seconds.

changeUser.title: Change this connector's user
changeUser.hint: It will act as this user, with their role. Nothing changes until the code is entered on the connector.
changeUser.codeBody: Enter this code on this connector's local page. It works once, until {{time}}, only on {{name}}, and isn't shown again.
changeUser.hintHeadless: It acts as this user at once, with their role. No code is needed, because nobody is at a machine with no screen.
changeUser.move: Move them to the new user

pair.title: Pair a device
pair.hint: The device will act as this user, with their role.

kindHint.desktop: You enter the code on its local page. It works once, for 10 minutes.
kindHint.headless: No screen needed: the code goes in a command or a compose file. It works once, for 24 hours.

code.title: Pairing code
code.body: Enter this code on the connector's local page. It works once, until {{time}}, and isn't shown again.

headless.title: Pair a NAS or server
headless.body: Use this code in one of the ways below. It works once, until {{time}}, and isn't shown again, so copy what you need before you close this.
headless.hubAddressHint: The address the NAS or server reaches this hub at. A machine on your network can't use localhost.
headless.dockerHint: Save this as docker-compose.connector.yml, then run the command under it. Host networking lets the connector hear Bambu printers announce themselves. Take the # off PUID and PGID, with your own numbers (run id over SSH, or see the NAS's user page), so the files it creates belong to you. Take it off the bind mount to share a folder; rslave makes a share mounted later show up inside.
headless.linuxHint: For a Raspberry Pi or a Linux server without Docker. Download the connector file for this version from the releases page (linux-arm64 on ARM), then run these. It needs systemd, and prints one sudo line if it can't keep running after you sign out.
headless.windowsHint: In an administrator PowerShell, in the folder with the setup file. It installs for all users and starts at boot with nobody signed in.
headless.windowsAccount: To run as a named account, which a network share needs, add these two. The password goes in the file, never on the command line:

pending.title: Unused pairing codes
pending.hint: A code for a NAS or server lasts 24 hours, longer than your visit here. Withdraw one you don't need: it pairs nothing after that.

settings.title: Sync
settings.deleteGuard: Pause after this many deletes at once
settings.deleteGuardHint: When a device deletes more files than this from one hub folder at once, its sync pauses and asks on the device's local page before anything moves to the hub's trash.
settings.defaultSyncModeHint: What a newly paired machine receives from the server to start with. Its picks are changed in Projects settings → Sources.
settings.versionsHint: When a device's save or an upload in the app replaces a hub file, the old content is kept. An upload into a machine's folder keeps it on that machine. Changes made directly on a disk are not kept. Backups include the hub's versions, so they grow.
settings.versionsKeepHint: Lowering this deletes the older versions on the hub now, and on a machine at a file's next upload.

presets.emptyBody: Turn on User presets Share for a machine on its page, or upload a slicer zip in Catalog settings → Sources. Their user presets join this library.
presets.noMatch: No preset of this type has that in its name.
presets.noneOfKind: No presets of this type yet.
presets.conflictsHint: A device saved its own version of a preset that had changed on the hub, so it was kept under a new name. Download both, keep what you need in your slicer, then delete the copy.
presets.deleteBody: It's removed from the hub's slicer, the slice workers and every device with Install on, unless a device's copy has edits it hasn't sent yet. Slices that used it need slicing again. On a PC signed in to Bambu Studio, delete it in the slicer too. Restore brings it back.
presets.removedInUse: Removed on {{devices}}, still in use: it goes once nothing uses it
presets.heldMass: Removed on {{device}} with many others at once: waits for you
presets.heldShared: Removed on {{device}}, whose slicer account another user's device shares: waits for you
presets.heldHint: A delete in a slicer reaches every device. These were held, because many went at once or because another user's device shares that slicer account, where a cloud sync can delete files nobody chose to delete. Delete them, or keep them: they're then written back to that device.
presets.heldSharedOn_one: {{device}} removed {{count}} preset on a shared slicer account
presets.heldSharedOn_other: {{device}} removed {{count}} presets on a shared slicer account
presets.deletedHint: Restore brings a preset back as its next version, and devices with Install on get it again.
presets.deviceOutdated: Its connector is older than the hub: its deletes only show here, and the hub's don't reach it. Update the connector.
presets.noBackup: No backup yet. One is made before the first write.
presets.editsStayLocal: This slicer's cloud account only takes new presets written to disk. An edit from the hub stays on this PC, and the cloud keeps the old version for other PCs.
presets.deleteHere_one: {{count}} preset deleted on the hub is still here. This slicer's cloud account brings back a file deleted from disk, so delete it in the slicer:
presets.deleteHere_other: {{count}} presets deleted on the hub are still here. This slicer's cloud account brings back a file deleted from disk, so delete them in the slicer:

machine.offline: Offline: changes apply when it reconnects.
machine.localPage: You're on this machine: open its local page
machine.stopReceivingBody: Its copies of hub projects are removed from the machine. Nothing is deleted on the hub.
machine.stopBody: It goes offline and starts again only when someone logs in on that computer or starts it by hand.
machine.stopped: Stopped. It shows offline in a few seconds.

errors.hubSlicer: This is the hub's slicer: its catalog is the hub's. Pick another in Integrations first.
errors.hubOff: Turn the hub on to reach printers or a spool library through a machine.
errors.slicingUnsupported: This machine can't slice: Bambu Studio and OrcaSlicer have no build for Linux on ARM.

machine.dockerUpdate: This connector runs in a container, so it doesn't update itself. In the folder with its compose file, run:
machine.cantSlice: A Linux machine on ARM can't be a slice worker: Bambu Studio and OrcaSlicer have no build for it. Slicing goes to a worker on x64, or a Mac.

held.line_one: {{name}}: {{count}} file deleted at once, and held
held.line_other: {{name}}: {{count}} files deleted at once, and held
held.confirmNamed: Delete the files held in {{name}} on the hub too
held.confirmTitle: Delete the files held in {{name}} on the hub too?
held.confirmBody: They move to the hub's trash, and every machine that receives this folder loses them. Restore keeps them instead.
held.restoring: Asked. The connector downloads them again.

machine.stopWorkerTitle: Stop using {{name}} as a server worker?
machine.stopWorkerBody: Its slicer installs in Integrations are removed, and a slicer the hub installed on it is uninstalled. What they imported stays. Turn this on again to set them up anew.
machine.reachPrintersName: Reach printers on this machine's network
machine.reachPrintersHint: Printers on this machine's network that the server can't reach itself. Its connector reads them for the server and never controls a printer.
machine.reachSpoolLibrariesName: Reach spool libraries on this machine's network
machine.reachSpoolLibrariesHint: Spool libraries on this machine's network that the server can't reach itself. Its connector reads their spools, and writes to one only the filament your prints used and the spools they used that it doesn't have yet.
machine.noPrinters: No printer goes through this machine.
machine.noSpoolLibraries: No spool library goes through this machine.
machine.stopReachBody: These are paused until you turn this on again and enable them in Integrations. They keep this machine.

system.title: System
system.waiting: Waiting for the connector's first report.
system.seenFrom: The hub sees this machine from {{address}}.
